subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated exec for cron and heartbeat be solved as a narrow per-job/per-heartbeat marker, or folded into the broader Gateway-owned scheduling and execution provenance model?
rationale: The unresolved behavior changes who may grant host exec authority to autonomous runs and likely touches cron protocol/storage, heartbeat runtime, audit, and upgrade semantics, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Treat this issue as part of a Gateway-owned scheduling/execution provenance contract that covers cron, heartbeat, approval receipts, audit, and migrations.

options.title: Narrow Cron/Heartbeat Marker
options.body: Add only a focused elevated marker for cron jobs and heartbeat runs, accepting a smaller patch with more follow-up security design remaining.

options.title: Defer Elevated Autonomy
options.body: Keep broad elevated exec unavailable to autonomous cron/heartbeat paths until the larger agent scheduling security model is ready.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as part of a Gateway-owned scheduling/execution provenance contract that covers cron, heartbeat, approval receipts, audit, and migrations.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on cron caller scoping is the closest current-main implementation boundary for the cron side of this security decision.
